KerML 1.0 8.2.2.1/3/5: form feed separates tokens; quoted names and strings share the seven Table 4 escapes and reject raw C0/C1 controls. Unicode diagnostic spans remain character-aligned and scanning retains complete source coverage and later declarations. Full Unicode printability and arbitrary line-terminator encodings remain unqualified. LEX-001–004, native syntax/round-trip checks and five lexer proof tests retain acceptance, refusal and recovery boundaries.

KERNEL-013: compose real literal values from their numeric tokens, excluding whitespace and notes while retaining exact original expression spans. KerML 8.2.2.1/4 and 8.2.5.8.4 define token separation and real composition. Decimal digits and exponents remain text with no floating-point conversion. Numeric syntax, AST/lowering regressions and LEX-006–009 retain acceptance, refusal and recovery boundaries.

KERNEL-013: enforce the existing decimal-scale allowance using an inclusive range check instead of signed absolute value, which overflows for i64::MIN. Extreme exponents remain syntactically valid but cannot wrap the exact-decimal reader into an incorrect finite result. Boundary regressions cover both signs, fractional scale adjustment, i64 limits and the unchanged 100000 allowance. This does not qualify real-valued cardinality or general expression evaluation.
